Saturday, 14 November 2026

  • Macro Dilemma—Soaring Growth vs. sticky CPI: The RBI raised India’s FY27 GDP forecast by 40 bps to 7.1% 19414 alongside record October exports of $49.5B 17854. However, October CPI breached the RBI’s 6% ceiling (at 6.09%) 19103 and trade deficits widened to $39.9B 19372, escalating expectations of a potential December repo rate hike 19335.
  • Global Turbulence & Tech Overhang: Global markets are reeling from aggressive Fed rate hike bets following elevated US PPI/CPI 1788917794. The surprise resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over a governance probe erased hundreds of billions in market value, dragging global tech sentiment 1076717967.
  • Foreign Capital Pivoting Back: Despite macro friction, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) executed a sharp U-turn, pumping up to ₹84,291 crore into domestic equities in November 1890919027. Global funds continue to rotate into India out of overextended AI markets 1896617412.
  • Tata Group Boardroom Friction: Governance disputes within Tata Trusts escalated as Vice-Chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh publicly defended N. Chandrasekaran’s leadership and the potential listing of Tata Sons, directly countering Noel Tata’s stance against prioritizing public listing profits 18759169717773.

Concurrently, massive capex commitments—such as Reliance’s ₹43,000 crore coal-to-gas plant 18203 and ₹80,000 crore renewable investments in AP 17850—underline strong industrial capex.

Market mood

Market sentiment remains cautious to sideways. While strong FPI inflows and solid underlying growth offer structural support, headline indices face near-term pressure from domestic rate-hike threats, sticky vegetable inflation, and global tech sell-offs following Nvidia’s executive departure. Expect sector-specific rotation rather than broad-based rallies.
